LensPin

How to add location to DSLR photos in Apple Photos

LensPin matches capture times to geotagged photos (photos with a saved location), a GPX file (a route with times and coordinates), or an Apple Health / Fitness workout route. Start with camera photos already imported into Apple Photos; optionally include videos.

From a trip to saved locations

  1. Choose a trip and camera

    Select photos directly or scan a date range, then choose a camera group. Photos with an existing location are skipped.

  2. Choose location sources

    Use iPhone photos, geotagged photos from another GPS-equipped camera, a GPX file, or an Apple Watch / Fitness workout route. HealthKit reads workout routes from Apple Health directly, with read-only access and no export needed.

  3. Check the camera clock

    Preview a fixed clock offset if the camera was fast, slow, or set to another time zone. Choose a time-zone display option separately. Neither changes the original capture time.

  4. Review before saving

    Inspect each suggestion’s map, reference photos, time gaps and whether the sources agree. Only the locations you approve are saved.

  5. Check the saved result

    Open the LensPin album in Apple Photos and check the map and coordinates. Added, Skipped and Failed are separate outcomes.

Four sources, one matching timeline

Photo references

LensPin uses geotagged photos from your iPhone or another GPS-equipped camera as reference points. Photos taken shortly before and after the camera photo are more helpful when their locations agree.

GPX and workout routes

Within a continuous part of the route, LensPin uses the photo’s time to estimate its position between recorded points. It does not bridge segment breaks or large gaps. Nearby photo locations can help reveal a conflict.

Understand the match categories

High Confidence

Clues are close in time and consistent. Selected by default, pending your confirmation.

Review

Clues may be sparse, one-sided or conflicting. Inspect the explanation before selecting.

No Clear Suggestion

The available clues are insufficient. Check the nearest references and leave the photo unchanged if you cannot confirm a place.

Saving and exporting

Saving locations to Apple Photos updates the library location and leaves original files unchanged. Existing locations are never overwritten. Optional JPG export creates a separate photo copy with GPS when “Include location” is enabled. Video GPS export is not supported.
